definitions.gloss: a-un; unspoken mutual understanding; perfect synchronization
definitions.explanation: Originally a Buddhist term representing the first and last sounds of the Sanskrit alphabet (like alpha and omega), symbolizing the beginning and end of all things. In modern usage, most commonly refers to the tacit, wordless coordination between two people who understand each other perfectly.

examples.japanese: {阿吽|あうん}の{呼吸|こきゅう}で{動|うご}く。
examples.english: To act in perfect unspoken harmony.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{相棒|あいぼう}とは{阿吽|あうん}の{呼吸|こきゅう}だ。
examples.english: With my long-time partner, we have perfect unspoken understanding.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}の{入口|いりぐち}には{阿吽|あうん}の{狛犬|こまいぬ}が{一対|いっつい}{置|お}かれている。
examples.english: At the entrance of shrines, a pair of guardian dogs — one with mouth open (a) and one closed (un) — are placed.

notes: Almost always used in the set phrase {阿吽|あうん}の{呼吸|こきゅう} (literally "a-un breathing"), meaning perfect wordless coordination. This phrase describes two people who work together so well they need no verbal communication. The concept originates in Buddhism: {阿|あ} (mouth open, the first sound) represents birth/beginning, and {吽|うん} (mouth closed, the last sound) represents death/ending. At shrines and temples, paired guardian statues ({狛犬|こまいぬ} or {仁王像|におうぞう}) embody this concept, with one figure's mouth open and the other closed.
